_comment: Authored, server-gradable practice items for the linear-algebra demo rail.
These exist because the gradable path was Postgres-only: /api/practice/item/:id
resolves through PgLearningObjectCatalog, nothing seeds generated_problems, and
demo/Dockerfile notes those tables are never created on the demo deploy. So a
DB-less instance — which is what an offline venue runs — had no gradable item at
all, and 'the win is earned on a real item' had nothing behind it.
Marking shape mirrors markingPayloadFromRow() in learning-object-catalog-pg.ts
exactly, so a file-backed item and a database row are indistinguishable to
GateDeterministicScorer. answerIndex indexes THIS options array, in this order.
Every answer here is checkable by hand in under a minute — that is deliberate.
A demo item whose correctness a visitor cannot verify themselves is a claim, not

items.question_text: A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]]. The eigenvalues of A are the roots of λ² − (trace)λ + (det) = 0. What are they?
A = [[3, 0], [0, 2]] is applied to the unit square. By what factor does the area scale?
solution_steps: The area scale factor of a linear map is |det(A)|.
The unit square maps to a 3 × 2 rectangle, area 6 — the same answer, seen directly.

items.question_text: Which vector is orthogonal to u = (3, 1)?
solution_steps: Two vectors are orthogonal exactly when their dot product is zero.
The others give 10, 20 and 6 — all non-zero, so none of them is perpendicular to u.
